cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Credit for the Impossible
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that you understood, predicted, or accepted the impossible truth before anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I drew that floating staircase last week. You used to laugh when I made you sketch what wasn't there yet. Tell them the date.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can all see it now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, your observation's caught up. I drew the handrail while you were explaining why stairs need support.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the voice I taught you to project. The people walking upstairs should hear who believed in their route before they could put a foot on it.

reason: Keep the exact impossible-premise Drive distinct: recruit a useful account, delegate a test, secure earlier-belief credit, force an explanatory choice, or request concrete premise-dependent action. Let old training shape that particular method.
